nodes.name: Disc Brake Pad
nodes.description: Friction lining component installed within disc brake calipers to generate stopping torque against the rotor.

evidence.quote: 3.  **Brake Pad Thickness:** Measure brake pad thickness and replace as needed.

nodes.name: Six-Bolt Rotor Mounting Standard
nodes.description: International standard specifying six M5 threaded bolts fastening the rotor disc to the hub shell flange.

evidence.quote:
The common system uses six bolts on a flange built into the hub shell.
Rotor-mounting bolts are M5 threading and typically use a Torx® T-25 size
wrench

nodes.name: Center Lock Rotor Mounting Standard
nodes.description: Splined hub mounting interface engineered to secure matching internally-splined disc brake rotors using a dedicated lockring.

interface_pattern.name: Spline Fitting Pattern
interface_pattern.note: Splined fittings with matching internal pattern

evidence.quote:
A “center-lock” hub is designed with splined fittings to accept rotors
made with a matching internal pattern. The rotor is held tight with a
lockring.

nodes.name: Center Lock Ring Torque Specification
nodes.description: Torque specification standard specifying 40 N·m tightening torque for Center Lock disc brake lockrings.

evidence.quote: *   **Center Lock Ring:** 40 N·m (as indicated on the lock ring itself). Verify with service manual.

nodes.name: Hydraulic Brake Lever
nodes.description: Handlebar-mounted master cylinder unit actuated by rider hand pressure to displace hydraulic fluid down to the caliper.

evidence.quote:
The brakes bleed from
caliper upward, and excess fluid exits at lever.

nodes.name: Brake Line
nodes.description: Bicycle brake line requiring care and caution during clamp usage.

handling_requirement.name: Hose Line Handling Caution
handling_requirement.note: be careful when using any brake lines

evidence.section: *   DOT FLUID, CAUSTIC MATERIAL. USE PROPER GLOVES.
evidence.quote: be careful when using any brake lines.

nodes.name: Hydraulic Caliper Bleed Procedure
nodes.description: Maintenance procedure establishing an uphill path from caliper upward to lever to purge air bubbles from the hydraulic system.

flow_direction.name: Purge Flow Path
flow_direction.note: uphill path from caliper body to lever

evidence.quote:
Procedure to bleed Tektro® caliper brakes:
a. Hold bike in repair stand and rotate bike so there is an uphill path from
caliper body to lever.

nodes.name: Hydraulic Brake Qualified Service Rule
nodes.description: Safety directive mandating specialized mechanical qualification prior to servicing high-pressure hydraulic bicycle brakes.

evidence.section: *   DOT FLUID, CAUSTIC MATERIAL. USE PROPER GLOVES.
evidence.quote: lic brake systems require specialized knowledge and skill. If you are not qualified, seek the assistance of a professional mechanic.

nodes.name: Brake Pad Fluid Contamination Safety Rule
nodes.description: Safety precaution requiring brake pad removal prior to hydraulic bleeding procedures to prevent oil contamination of friction materials.

pad_removal_on_bleed.name: Pad Removal Requirement
pad_removal_on_bleed.note: best to remove pads to avoid contamination

evidence.quote:
While the system can be bled with brake pads in place, it is best to remove
pads to avoid any chance of contamination with brake fluid.
